latest_apis.rationale: Otherwise consistently current-generation Nuxt 4 (useAsyncData+watch, useHead, useState, script setup, app/ layout), but the one systematic miss is real: Nuxt 4.6 — the version installed — introduced nuxt/server and ships its own auto-imported setResponseStatus precisely to decouple from h3 before Nuxt 5's h3 v2 (nuxt.com/blog/v4-6), yet all 5 pages import from h3 directly.

app/app/composables/useApiBase.ts:1-9 — API base resolved in one place, synced server→client via useState payload

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and configuration are each centralized behind one module, so most requirement changes touch one file — genuinely good. But the h3 import spread over five pages, any-typed API records at the boundary, and the copy-pasted title suffix are exactly the kind of thing that ripples at a framework major.

findings.issue: setResponseStatus imported from 'h3' in all five page components (also moves/[name].vue:2, abilities/[name].vue:2, types/[name].vue:2, [...slug].vue:2), coupling app code to h3 v1's event shape; Nuxt 4.6 ships nuxt/server and its own auto-imported setResponseStatus composable precisely so this code survives Nuxt 5's move to h3 v2
findings.suggestion: Drop the h3 import and use the Nuxt-native (auto-imported) setResponseStatus, or import from 'nuxt/server' for portability; the Nuxt 4.6 blog documents this as the upgrade path

findings.issue: API responses are typed `any` at the one module that guards the boundary (Promise<any> cache at pokeapi.ts:48, `as any`/`(t: any)` casts throughout the page loaders), so API schema changes surface as runtime undefineds instead of type errors
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API record shapes actually consumed (NamedRef already exists) and let api() return them; keep the domain view models as-is

findings.issue: The fetch promise is stored in the cache before it settles, so a transient network error caches a rejected promise for the server process lifetime, permanently failing that resource
findings.suggestion: cache.delete(url) in a .catch() on the stored promise (or store settled results) so a failure can be retried

findings.issue: compatibilityDate '2025-07-15' pins a ~15-month-old behavior window instead of the current one; Nuxt sets it to the current date on project creation
findings.suggestion: Bump compatibilityDate to the present (or the Nuxt 4.6-era date) and rely on the documented migration notes when behavior flags change

findings.issue: The '– Pokédex' title suffix is hand-concatenated in six files (types/index.vue:4, [..slug].vue:4, moves/abilities/types/[name].vue), duplicating a cross-cutting convention
findings.suggestion: Set titleTemplate: '%s – Pokédex' once (nuxt.config.ts app.head or app.vue) and have pages set only their title

findings.issue: vue and vue-router are declared as direct dependencies but never imported directly anywhere in app/app (auto-imports only); they are transitive deps of nuxt
findings.suggestion: Remove them, or keep only if deliberately pinning versions ahead of Nuxt's resolution — as-is they add nothing

findings.issue: URLs are built by string concatenation with a manual trailing-slash strip, and parsed with a regex at pokeapi.ts:20, where the URL API is available and handles these cases natively
findings.suggestion: Use new URL(path, base) for building and new URL(url).pathname for idFromUrl

summary: A lean, current-generation Nuxt 4.6 app: one well-defined data-access module, native fetch, zero gratuitous dependencies, and modern Nuxt idioms everywhere except one systematic pattern — importing setResponseStatus from h3 in five page components, which Nuxt 4.6's new nuxt/server surface and own composable exist specifically to replace ahead of the h3 v2 / Nuxt 5 jump. Combined with a stale compatibilityDate, any-typed API records at the otherwise-clean boundary, and a permanently-cached rejected-promise edge case, it will age acceptably but needs a small, well-contained pass before the next framework major.

apis.replacement: Nuxt's own auto-imported setResponseStatus composable (#app/composables/ssr, already in the project's .nuxt/types/imports.d.ts), or 'nuxt/server' for portability across h3/Nitro majors — see nuxt.com/blog/v4-6
